name: Guidelines for Pump Installation (Table 4.1.1)
description: Table 4.1.1 containing installation guidelines and explanations.

name: Make sure that the space around the unit is sufficient.
description: This facilitates ventilation, inspection, maintenance, and service.

name: If you require lifting equipment such as a hoist or tackle, make sure that there is enough space above the pump.
description: This makes it easier to properly use the lifting equipment and safely remove and relocate the components to a safe location.

name: Protect the unit from weather and water damage due to rain, flooding, and freezing temperatures.
description: This is applicable if nothing else is specified.

name: Do not install and operate the equipment in closed systems unless the system is constructed with properly-sized safety devices and control devices.
description: Acceptable devices: Pressure relief valves, Pressure controls, Temperature controls, Flow controls. If the system does not include these devices, consult the engineer or architect in charge before you operate the pump.

name: Take into consideration the occurrence of unwanted noise and vibration.
Make sure that the unit location is on solid, level ground.
description: This ensures that the unit remains stable and balanced while in operation.

name: Table 4.2.1 - Piping Installation Checklist
description: Checklist of piping installation checks for pump systems.

name: Check that all piping is supported independently of, and lined up naturally with, the pump connection.
description:
This helps to prevent:
• Strain on the pump
• Misalignment between the pump and the drive unit
• Wear on the pump bearings, seal, and shafting
See Example section for illustrations of pipe supports.

name: Check that only necessary fittings are used.
description: This helps to minimize friction losses.

name: Make sure that all the piping joints and fittings are airtight.
description: This prevents air from entering the piping system or leaks that occur during operation.

name: If the pump handles corrosive fluids, make sure that the piping allows you to flush out the liquid before you remove the pump.
description: This protects the employees and operators.

name: If the pump handles liquids at elevated temperatures, make sure that the expansion loops and joints are properly installed.
description: This helps to prevent misalignment due to thermal expansion of the piping.

name: If the pump handles corrosive liquids, make sure that the piping is correctly rated for the application.

• Pressurized device. Make sure that the internal pressure is relieved before you continue.
• Compressed Gas Hazard. Never apply a pressure to any cavity or chamber in the
product to test for leakage. Pressurized air may cause parts to be propelled with force.
Overpressurization can cause structural failure.
• Make sure that the pump is isolated from the system and that pressure is relieved before
you disassemble the pump, remove plugs, open vent or drain valves, or disconnect the piping.
• Maintenance and service must be performed by skilled and qualified personnel only.

name: [CAUTION] Allow all system and pump components to cool before you…

• Read all operation and maintenance manuals supplied with the unit.
